- the target is not empty, but the cutter-centre area after the erosion by the tool radius is empty (the open area is narrower than the tool).

Found while working #1706.

title: finish3d: a straight link across gap openings (gap_link: Jump, Straight)
body:
What the user asked for (chat, 2026-11-14): "i want it to form a smooth link move over holes in the surface. lets start with a straight line between each edge of the hole. later we can add splines and curves for how to connect them."

What happens now: finish3d (Parallel and the other march patterns) breaks a raster line where the tool cannot stand, for example over a hole. The chain between the two runs lifts to the retract plane. The tool makes an air hop for every gap. On a part with many holes this is slow and the moves look wrong in the GUI.

Change: add an operation parameter `gap_link` to the finishing parameters. The parameter is a dropdown with two options:

- `Jump` (default): today's behaviour, unchanged. The chain lifts to the retract plane.
- `Straight`: one straight Feed move between the end of one run and the start of the next, at the two end points' own tip height.

Law for `Straight`: both run ends stand at tangent centers by the march construction. The author certifies the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS`. A grazing contact at the rim passes. A real bite refuses. On a refusal the chain takes the `Jump` hop. No air margin is added for `Straight`; `Jump` keeps its own retract law.

Also fixed, needed by this feature: the raster serpentine ran a broken back line wrong. It reversed only each piece's points and kept the pieces in grid order. Every gap link then jumped back across the field instead of crossing its gap. A back line now reverses whole: the pieces in reverse order, and each piece's points reversed. This also shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines.

How the parameter is stored: the project digest takes a `0x4D` tag plus a variant byte only when `gap_link` is not `Jump`. The project file grammar takes the words `jump` and `straight`. No project-file version step-up. The MCP params door and the UI combo carry the same two options.

Done means:

- The Gap link dropdown offers Jump and Straight; Jump is the default and writes the old bytes.
- Over a holed plate, `Straight` authors rim-to-rim Feed links at the run height and no retract hop for those gaps.
- A `Straight` link that would cut the part is refused, and the hop stands (Prime Directive).
- Every gap crossing on a broken back line spans one gap, never the field.
- Pins: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs`, the round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`, and the MCP params-door test.

## What happens

`cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lead_approach` fails 2 tests on upstream/main b6c02115:

- `the_reported_keep_down_helix_pocket_enters_every_level_once`
- `the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`

Both stop at line 108: `the stock-source pocket cuts the user's part: []`.

## Cause

Commit 086f4010 (#1603) made the helper `beside_the_cut_part` assert that the stock-source pocket on `Milling-test.step` cuts the part. At that time the pocket cut through the part.

PR #1656 (#1554) merged at 12:16Z. It makes a stock-source pocket clear the stock around the part. So the pocket no longer cuts the part, and the assertion is now wrong. The new behaviour is correct.

## Fix

Change the helper to assert that the stock-source pocket has no `Gouge`. Keep the entry-law checks on the remaining warnings.

body:
**What happens:** since #1603 (stock-source pocket family), #1607 (every stock-source 2D kind with a part law) and #1621 (a part-source op against the setup's other parts, PR #1622), an operation's verdict is read against parts BESIDE its source (`keep_law::parts_in_stock`, `keep_law::neighbour_parts`). The op's stamp (`operation::stamp::current_stamp`) still digests only the source (plus the stock for a non-stock source). So after a clean generation, a part that is moved into the cut, added, un-tagged as a fixture, or un-marked as raw stock only leaves the op `Ok` with a verdict nobody gave.

- Aligned stock: the program sim judges every part live at post and refuses.
- **Turned stock** (the sim refuses to judge): the post reads the ops' cached verdicts - all `Ok` and clean - and the program goes out into the moved part. Same hole the original #1603 / #1607 / #1621 fixes closed, re-opened by an edit after generation.

The other direction is fail-safe but confusing: marking a casting raw stock only (#1094) or moving a neighbour away leaves the op `Ok` with its old gouges cached; the post refuses until the user regenerates for no visible reason.

**Tried on PR #1622 and pulled back** (branch `issue/1607-stock-source-law`: f4d86b41 and 6abccc77 add it, the commit after dae97790 takes it out again): a stamp term digesting the kept set (`name`, `setup_align::pose_in`, `model::geometry_signature` of each model the part laws read; written only when the set is non-empty). It works (pinned: moving the neighbour makes the op Stale; red without the term), but it breaks established stamp contracts that need a maintainer's call:
- `fixtures.rs::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath` - un-tagging a vise turns it into a part, so the op goes Stale (the "workholding never stales" law, M2.3).
- `operations.rs::a_frommodel_stock_survives_its_source_being_deleted` and `a_model_update_does_not_touch_a_box_stock` - "a stock-based path never reads the model": a stock-source Face now does (its parts).
- `fidelity_copies.rs` (2 tests) - deleting the stock's coarse source model makes the stock-source op Stale, so the gate says "regenerate" instead of the named fidelity refusal.
- `stock_source_verdict.rs` - marking the casting raw stock only stales a part-source op.

**Options:** (a) the stamp term above, restating those contracts (the kept parts are inputs; workholding stays out only while it is tagged); (b) no stamp term, but the post re-reads the part laws live for ops whose kept set changed (like the workholding gate does), so nothing churns; (c) (b) only when the sim cannot judge.

Found while fixing #1621 (PR #1622; `docs/decisions/1607-stock-source-law.md`).

Done means: a part moved into a stock-source or part-source op's cut after generation never posts on a turned stock (refused by name, Stale or live re-judgement); the chosen option's contract changes are decided and recorded; pinned and mutation-checked.

**Found in a PathPilot Hub run (770MX sim, v2.14.4, 2026-11-13)** of the merged #1357 golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/drill_peck.nc`, posted inch for the 770MX.

**What happened.** In Hub's tool table T4 is 5.0000" long. With the session's G54 Z zero, the top of Z travel was only about 4.3" above work Z0. The program runs:

```
G53 G0 Z0        (top of travel)
G30
T4 M6
G43 H4           (5" tool: the tip is now about 0.68" BELOW work Z0, though nothing moved)
S1500 M3
M8
G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937       <- the XY traverse at that height: below the part top
G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937 Z0    <- then UP to Z0
```

The user saw the tool go down, then over, then up. "Down" is the 5" length offset taking effect. "Over" is the XY rapid with the tip about 0.68" below the stock surface. "Up" is the rapid to Z0. On a real machine that traverse would drive the tool through the part or the vise. At load time PathPilot warned "Program exceeds machine maximum on Z axis by 0.5107 in (line 0)", but the post still writes a traverse that cannot clear.

**Cause.** `tormach.cps` (`xyFirst` / `startXY`) makes the first XY move after a tool change "at the current - safe, Z-up - height". It assumes the top of travel is above the part. It never states the section's clearance Z before the traverse. When the tool is too long for the work offset, the top of travel is below that clearance.

**Proposed fix.** After `G43 H..`, and before the first XY traverse, write `G0 Z<clearance>` from the section's `ClearancePlane` (or its first rapid's Z). On a setup that can clear, this is an ordinary move down to clearance. On a setup that cannot, the control refuses the block as beyond its Z limit and stops. That is a visible refusal, not a rapid through the part. Pin it with a test: a stream whose first XY rapid follows a tool change shows `G0 Z<clearance>` before it. Regenerate the Tormach goldens this moves (listed in the PR). Check whether the other mill posts share the assumption, and file each one that does.

**Done means:** no Tormach program makes its first XY traverse after a tool change without first stating the clearance Z. That is pinned by a test, and the moved goldens are listed in the PR.

title: Process: the PR review compares 3-5 named risk spots against their reference instead of sampling; a PR sent back twice escalates its effort tier

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
**What happens.** The `PR-reviewer` checks a PR against the laws (unwrap, commands, layering, placement, process) and runs the touched suites, but nothing tells it *where* a behaviour bug is most likely or what to compare the new code with. With a large diff it ends up sampling. And there is no bound on review rounds: a PR can go `needs-rework` -> fix -> full review -> `needs-rework` again, each round on the same (possibly too cheap) worker tier and each round a full review build.

**Evidence.** In another agent-driven Rust project of this contributor, run with the same builder -> reviewer setup, an evaluation on 2026-11-12 found that reviews without named spots took samples and found nothing; the one real finding of the period came only when the dispatcher named the risky places and the reference function to compare with. The same project caps the loop at one rework per tier.

**Proposal (process files only):**
1. `work-issue` step 5: the draft PR body carries a `Risk spots:` list - 3-5 entries, each `file:function - what could go wrong - reference` (the issue's Done means, the public source in the module's provenance line, or the existing function / law the change mirrors). Typical spots: new geometry or formulas, anything that reaches posted G-code, file/project writing and round-trip, state across frames, undo/redo and abort paths.
2. `PR-reviewer` step 5: a new first item "Risk spots, not samples": take the PR's list (or choose 3-5 itself when it is missing), read each hunk and its reference, compare step by step, and name in the review what each spot was compared with.
3. AGENTS.md "Escalation, never silent" and `work-issue` step 4: a PR whose second full review is again `needs-rework` is not reworked a third time on the same tier - the issue's effort label rises one step and the next rework goes to that tier (`max`: `blocked`, maintainer decides).
4. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` +1.

Suggested labels: `P5`, `effort:low`, `source:agent` (the contributor cannot set labels).

**Done means:** the four files carry the rules above; a fork that syncs to the new PROCESS_VERSION gets them; #681 has the announcement line when it merges.

Part of #866. Related: #637 (carried stock on the field engine), #586.

**What the reporter wanted:** a plate modelled lying flat; Setup1 machines it flat, Setup2 stands it on its edge (part alignment "turned X -90°") and takes "What Setup1 leaves behind" as its stock. Today that carry is refused by design (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`): the carried body is a two-sided column lattice (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`, `LatticeTurn`), which can only be re-indexed through flips over X or Y and quarter turns about Z. A side-on turn would need a re-sample at the grid pitch, and the sim refuses rather than guess.

Investigation for #866 confirmed the frame composition is right: `setup_relative::transform_between` uses the RELATIVE turn (`A_to * A_from^-1`), so two setups holding the part alike (both turned X -90°) carry fine (pinned by `setup_stock_source::both_setups_turned_alike_carry_through_the_identity`). Only a real side-on turn between the setups is refused.

**The work:** carry the machined stock through any rigid turn between setups (at least the side-on quarter turns about X and Y - the common "machine the edge" re-clamp), once the carried body lives on the field engine (#637), with the verdicts proven exact enough and the named refusal kept for anything the engine still cannot carry.

**Done means:** Setup1 flat, Setup2 turned 90° about X (or Y) with "What Setup1 leaves behind" simulates, judges gouges and feeds rest/judged stock from the carried body; a pinning test carries a faced plate side-on and checks its volume and verdict.
